title: Hom exactness for sequential finite-free colimits with a Mittag-Leffler kernel system
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $G_n$ be $R$-modules with $R$-linear maps $u_n:G_n\to G_{n+1}$ for integers $n\ge1$, and suppose $G_n\cong R^{r_n}$ for finite integers $r_n\ge0$. Let compatible maps $\iota_n:G_n\to P$ exhibit an $R$-module $P$ as their colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For an $R$-module $N$ put $L_N=\{(h_n)\in\prod_{n\ge1}\operatorname{Hom}_R(G_n,N):h_{n+1}u_n=h_n\text{ for every }n\}$, with componentwise $R$-module operations. Restriction gives an $R$-linear isomorphism $\rho_N:\operatorname{Hom}_R(P,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}L_N$, $h\mapsto(h\iota_n)_n$. These isomorphisms are natural in $N$: for every $v:N\to N^\prime$, $\rho_{N^\prime}(vh)=(v h\iota_n)_n$. If $0\to N_1\xrightarrow{a}N_2\xrightarrow{b}N_3\to0$ is a short exact sequence of $R$-modules (meaning $a$ is injective, $b$ is surjective and $\operatorname{im}a=\ker b$), and the inverse sequence $\operatorname{Hom}_R(G_n,N_1)$ with precomposition transitions $h\mapsto h u_n$ is Mittag-Leffler [def-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-system], then $0\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(P,N_1)\xrightarrow{a\circ-}\operatorname{Hom}_R(P,N_2)\xrightarrow{b\circ-}\operatorname{Hom}_R(P,N_3)\to0$ is short exact.

proof.text: For each $N$, restriction is well-defined: $(h\iota_{n+1})u_n=h\iota_n$ by cocone compatibility. It preserves addition and scalar multiplication componentwise. Conversely, for $(h_n)\in L_N$, its adjacent compatibility implies compatibility with all composites by induction on the number of transitions. Thus it is a cocone to $N$ on the small category of positive integers. The colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives a unique linear map $h:P\to N$ with $h\iota_n=h_n$. This proves bijectivity of $\rho_N$; since it is linear, its inverse is linear as well.

proof.text: For $v:N\to N^\prime$, associativity gives $\rho_{N^\prime}(vh)_n=(vh)\iota_n=v(h\iota_n)$. Postcomposition $v_*:(h_n)\mapsto(vh_n)$ preserves compatibility since $(vh_{n+1})u_n=v(h_{n+1}u_n)=vh_n$. Hence $\rho_{N^\prime}\circ(v\circ-)=v_*\circ\rho_N$, which proves the asserted naturality.

proof.text: Fix $n$ and put $H_{i,n}=\operatorname{Hom}_R(G_n,N_i)$, $A_n(f)=af$ and $B_n(g)=bg$. The row $0\to H_{1,n}\xrightarrow{A_n}H_{2,n}\xrightarrow{B_n}H_{3,n}\to0$ is exact directly: injectivity of $a$ implies injectivity of $A_n$; if $bg=0$, the unique pointwise preimage $f(x)$ defined by $af(x)=g(x)$ exists by $\operatorname{im}a=\ker b$ and is linear by injectivity of $a$. Conversely $baf=0$. Finally choose a basis $e_1,\ldots,e_{r_n}$ of $G_n$, lift each value $k(e_j)$ through the surjection $b$, and extend these finitely many lifts linearly to obtain $g$ with $bg=k$. This also covers $r_n=0$, using the empty basis.

source.place: Tag 059X (lemma-countgen-projective), finite-free Hom rows and final functorial colimit identification; Tag 0598 (lemma-ML-exact-sequence).

proof.text: Use precomposition by $u_n$ as the transition $H_{i,n+1}\to H_{i,n}$. The squares commute because $(af)u_n=a(fu_n)$ and $(bg)u_n=b(gu_n)$. The rows of step 3 therefore form a short exact sequence of inverse systems of underlying abelian groups indexed by the positive integers. Its kernel system $(H_{1,n})$ is ML by the stated hypothesis [def-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-system]. Apply part (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-limit-exact]: its compatible-sequence limit is exactly $L_{N_i}$. Thus $0\to L_{N_1}\xrightarrow{a_*}L_{N_2}\xrightarrow{b_*}L_{N_3}\to0$ is exact. These induced maps are $R$-linear by their coordinate formulas, so exactness of underlying abelian groups gives exactness of these modules.

source.place: Tag 059X (lemma-countgen-projective), finite-free Hom rows and final functorial colimit identification; Tag 0598 (lemma-ML-exact-sequence).

proof.text: By step 2 the maps on these limits satisfy $\rho_{N_2}(af)=a_*\rho_{N_1}(f)$ and $\rho_{N_3}(bg)=b_*\rho_{N_2}(g)$. Injectivity of $a_*$ and bijectivity of the $\rho$ imply injectivity of $a\circ-$. If $bg=0$, step 4 supplies $x\in L_{N_1}$ with $a_*x=\rho_{N_2}(g)$; setting $f=\rho_{N_1}^{-1}(x)$ gives $af=g$, and the reverse inclusion in the kernel follows from $ba=0$. Given $k:P\to N_3$, choose $y\in L_{N_2}$ with $b_*y=\rho_{N_3}(k)$ and put $g=\rho_{N_2}^{-1}(y)$; then $bg=k$. This proves every clause of the required short exactness.

lean.statement: theorem sequential_free_colimit_hom_exact {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (F : ℕ ⥤ ModuleCat.{v} R) (hfree : ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ r : ℕ, Nonempty (F.obj n ≃ₗ[R] (Fin r → R))) (c : Cocone F) (hc : IsColimit c) : (∃ ρ : (N : ModuleCat.{w} R) → (c.pt →ₗ[R] N) ≃ₗ[R] ModuleCat.sectionsSubmodule (sequentialHomSystem F N), (∀ (N : ModuleCat.{w} R) (h : c.pt →ₗ[R] N) (n : ℕ), (ρ N h).val (Opposite.op n) = h.comp (c.ι.app n).hom) ∧ (∀ (N N' : ModuleCat.{w} R) (a : N →ₗ[R] N') (h : c.pt →ₗ[R] N) (n : ℕ), (ρ N' (a.comp h)).val (Opposite.op n) = a.comp ((ρ N h).val (Opposite.op n)))) ∧ (∀ (N₁ : ModuleCat.{w₁} R) (N₂ : ModuleCat.{w₂} R) (N₃ : ModuleCat.{w₃} R) (a : N₁ →ₗ[R] N₂) (b : N₂ →ₗ[R] N₃), Function.Injective a → Function.Exact a b → Function.Surjective b → (sequentialHomSystem F N₁ ⋙ forget (ModuleCat R)).IsMittagLeffler → Function.Injective (fun h : c.pt →ₗ[R] N₁ ↦ a.comp h) ∧ Function.Exact (fun h : c.pt →ₗ[R] N₁ ↦ a.comp h) (fun h : c.pt →ₗ[R] N₂ ↦ b.comp h) ∧ Function.Surjective (fun h : c.pt →ₗ[R] N₂ ↦ b.comp h))
